statements.status_notes: CVE-2025-15661 is a heap buffer over-read in sftp_symlink() in src/sftp.c of libssh2 through 1.11.1: a malicious SFTP server or a man-in-the-middle can answer a READLINK or REALPATH request with an SSH_FXP_NAME reply whose link length exceeds the packet, disclosing client heap memory or crashing the client. Upstream fixed it in https://github.com/libssh2/libssh2/commit/2dae3024897e1898d389835151f4e9606227721d which makes sftp_symlink() read the reply through bounds-checked buffer helpers. Alpine lists it as fixed in its own 1.11.1-r4 in the secfixes of its libssh2 recipe: https://gitlab.alpinelinux.org/alpine/aports/-/blob/3.23-stable/main/libssh2/APKBUILD . This owner's 1.11.1-r4 carries a backport of the upstream commit on top of Alpine's 1.11.1-r3 recipe, and 1.11.1-r5 is built from Alpine's 1.11.1-r4 recipe, which carries the same fix. We checked every published libssh2 build for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository, 1.11.1-r1 to 1.11.1-r5, on x86_64 and aarch64, each verified against its index checksum: the shared library /usr/lib/libssh2.so.1.0.1 (libssh2) and the static library /usr/lib/libssh2.a (libssh2-static). The error messages the fix adds to sftp_symlink(), "SFTP Protocol Error (type)", "SFTP Protocol Error (code)" and "SFTP Protocol Error (filename)", are present in both libraries in 1.11.1-r4 and 1.11.1-r5 and absent from 1.11.1-r1, 1.11.1-r2 and 1.11.1-r3, while the message "no name entries" from the same function is found in every build checked. 1.11.1-r4 is the first fixed build; 1.11.1-r1, 1.11.1-r2 and 1.11.1-r3 are affected.

statements.impact_statement: CVE-2025-15661: libssh2 through 1.11.1 reads past a heap buffer in sftp_symlink() (src/sftp.c) when an SFTP server sends an SSH_FXP_NAME reply whose link length is larger than the packet, which can disclose heap memory or crash the client. It is fixed by libssh2 commit 2dae302: https://github.com/libssh2/libssh2/commit/2dae3024897e1898d389835151f4e9606227721d, https://github.com/libssh2/libssh2/pull/1717. Two builds of this owner are published in the DHI Alpine 3.24 repository, 1.96.0-r0 and 1.96.1-r0, each as the rust and cargo packages for x86_64 and aarch64; every file of all eight packages was scanned. Only cargo contains libssh2 code. In 1.96.0-r0, /usr/bin/cargo has libssh2 compiled in statically through the libssh2-sys 0.3.1 crate, but only libssh2's transport, channel and authentication code is linked: the program contains most of the error messages of libssh2 1.11.1's src/userauth.c and src/session.c and many of src/channel.c, but none of the error messages specific to src/sftp.c; the only src/sftp.c message text present is the generic prefix Unable to allocate memory for, which src/channel.c and src/userauth.c also use. None of sftp_symlink()'s own messages, such as SFTP symlink packet too short or Unable to send SYMLINK/READLINK command, is present. In 1.96.1-r0, cargo is linked against the system libssh2 (it needs libssh2.so.1, supplied by the separate libssh2 package) and contains no copy of libssh2. Alpine made that change in its rust 1.96.1-r0 recipe and lists it as its fix for this CVE: https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/commit/0f7dfa74845f47bc7ae7251e07fd7d68716870b8. The rust package contains no libssh2 code. No published build of this owner contains sftp_symlink().

statements.status_notes: CVE-2025-15661 is a heap buffer over-read in sftp_symlink() in src/sftp.c of libssh2 through 1.11.1: a malicious SFTP server or a man-in-the-middle can answer a READLINK or REALPATH request with an SSH_FXP_NAME reply whose link length exceeds the packet, disclosing client heap memory or crashing the client. Upstream fixed it in https://github.com/libssh2/libssh2/commit/2dae3024897e1898d389835151f4e9606227721d which makes sftp_symlink() read the reply through bounds-checked buffer helpers. Debian fixed it for trixie in 1.11.1-1+deb13u1, DSA-6365-1: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2025-15661 . We checked every published libssh2 build for Debian 13 in the DHI Debian repository rebuilt from Debian 1.11.1-1+deb13u1 or 1.11.1-1+deb13u2 (four builds), on amd64 and arm64, each verified against its index checksum: the shared library libssh2.so.1.0.1 (libssh2-1t64) and the static library libssh2.a (libssh2-1-dev). Each build's Debian changelog includes the 1.11.1-1+deb13u1 security update entry naming this CVE, and the error messages the fix adds to sftp_symlink(), "SFTP Protocol Error (type)", "SFTP Protocol Error (code)" and "SFTP Protocol Error (filename)", are present in both libraries in each of these builds, on both architectures, while the message "no name entries" from the same function is found in every build checked. The fixed version is the first DHI build of 1.11.1-1+deb13u1, and every later build carries the fix.
